# Employment Contract Templates — Skill Documentation Overview & Workflow

This documentation summary walks you through the skill available in this workspace for creating employment documents, with special attention to your use case: a **Senior Software Engineer offer letter**.

---

## Skill Purpose

This skill provides **templates and patterns** for creating legally sound employment documentation:

- Employment contracts
- Offer letters
- Employee handbooks
- HR policies
- NDAs and non-competes
- Onboarding documentation

### When to Use

- Drafting employment contracts
- Creating offer letters
- Writing employee handbooks
- Developing HR policies
- Standardizing employment documentation
- Onboarding documentation

---

## Core Concepts

### Employment Document Types

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** | Initial job offer | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal agreement | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies & procedures | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality | Before access |
| **Non-Compete** | Competition restriction | Hire/Exit |

### Key Legal Considerations

```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

> **DISCLAIMER:** These templates are for informational purposes only and do not constitute legal advice. Consult with qualified legal counsel before using any employment documents.

---

## Documentation Overview — Templates Available

The skill includes three primary templates:

### Template 1: Offer Letter
A full offer letter with sections for:

- Position details (title, department, reports-to, location, start date, employment type)
- Compensation (salary, bonus, equity)
- Benefits (health, 401(k), PTO, holidays)
- Contingencies (background check, work authorization, execution of required documents)
- At-will employment language
- Acceptance signature block

### Template 2: Employment Agreement (Contract Position)
A more formal, comprehensive employment agreement:

- Employment duties and location
- Employment term (at-will or fixed-term options)
- Base salary, bonus, equity, benefits, expenses
- Confidentiality obligations
- Intellectual property assignment
- Non-competition and non-solicitation clauses
- Termination provisions and severance
- General legal provisions (entire agreement, amendments, governing law, dispute resolution, severability, notices, assignment, waiver)
- Execution signatures and Exhibit A for prior inventions

### Template 3: Employee Handbook Policy Section
Policy language covering:

- Equal Employment Opportunity
- Anti-harassment / reporting / investigation
- Work hours and attendance
- PTO accrual and guidelines
- Sick leave
- Holidays
- Code of conduct
- Technology and communication acceptable use
- Social media policy
- Employee acknowledgment form

---

## Workflow Guidance

Use the following process to create a Senior Software Engineer offer letter.

### Step 1 — Confirm the document type

For a new hire offer, the appropriate document is:

> **Offer Letter** (Template 1)

A Senior Software Engineer role may also involve signing an **Employment Agreement**, **Confidentiality/NDA**, and **IP Assignment Agreement** at a later stage, but the initial offer document is the offer letter.

### Step 2 — Gather the required data

Collect all relevant details before drafting:

| Data Category | Example for Senior Software Engineer |
|---------------|--------------------------------------|
| Company legal name and letterhead | [Company Name] |
| Candidate full name and address | [Full name/address] |
| Job title | Senior Software Engineer |
| Department | Engineering |
| Reports to | VP Engineering / Engineering Manager |
| Location | Office / Hybrid / Remote |
| Start date | [Date] |
| Employment type | Full-Time, Exempt |
| Base salary | $[Amount]/year |
| Bonus | [Discretionary %, if applicable] |
| Equity | [Shares/options, if offered] |
| Benefits | Health, 401(k), PTO, holidays |
| Contingencies | Background check, authorization, NDAs |
| Acceptance deadline | [Date] |
| HR contact | [Name/email/phone] |

### Step 3 — Use the Offer Letter template

Open the **Offer Letter template** and replace all bracketed placeholders. The full template is included below. For a Senior Software Engineer, ensure:

- Title = `Senior Software Engineer`
- Department = `Engineering`
- Contingencies include confidentiality, IP assignment, and background check as appropriate
- At-will language is included if applicable

### Step 4 — Customize with role-specific language

Senior Software Engineer positions often involve heightened intellectual property and confidentiality concerns. Include relevant contingency documents:

- Confidentiality Agreement
- IP Assignment Agreement
- Non-Compete Agreement (if applicable and lawful in your jurisdiction)
- Background check requirement

### Step 5 — Legal review

Employment law varies by jurisdiction. Confirm:

- Exempt/non-exempt classification for the salary threshold
- At-will language requirements
- Non-compete enforceability in the candidate’s state
- Any state-specific required notices or benefit rules

### Step 6 — Finalize and obtain acceptance

Print the deadline clearly. Include the acceptance signature section. Execute and retain signed copies.

---

## Offer Letter Template — Full Reference

Use this template from the skill documentation to draft your Senior Software Engineer offer letter:

```markdown
# EMPLOYMENT OFFER LETTER

[Company Letterhead]

Date: [DATE]

[Candidate Name]
[Address]
[City, State ZIP]

Dear [Candidate Name],

We are pleased to extend an offer of employment for the position of [JOB TITLE]
at [COMPANY NAME]. We believe your skills and experience will be valuable
additions to our team.

## Position Details

**Title:** [Job Title]
**Department:** [Department]
**Reports To:** [Manager Name/Title]
**Location:** [Office Location / Remote]
**Start Date:** [Proposed Start Date]
**Employment Type:** [Full-Time/Part-Time], [Exempt/Non-Exempt]

## Compensation

**Base Salary:** $[AMOUNT] per [year/hour], paid [bi-weekly/semi-monthly/monthly]
**Bonus:** [Eligible for annual bonus of up to X% based on company and individual
performance / Not applicable]
**Equity:** [X shares of stock options vesting over 4 years with 1-year cliff /
Not applicable]

## Benefits

You will be eligible for our standard benefits package, including:
- Health insurance (medical, dental, vision) effective [date]
- 401(k) with [X]% company match
- [X] days paid time off per year
- [X] paid holidays
- [Other benefits]

Full details will be provided during onboarding.

## Contingencies

This offer is contingent upon:
- Successful completion of background check
- Verification of your right to work in [Country]
- Execution of required employment documents including:
  - Confidentiality Agreement
  - [Non-Compete Agreement, if applicable]
  - [IP Assignment Agreement]

## At-Will Employment

Please note that employment with [Company Name] is at-will. This means that
either you or the Company may terminate the employment relationship at any time,
with or without cause or notice. This offer letter does not constitute a
contract of employment for any specific period.

## Acceptance

To accept this offer, please sign below and return by [DEADLINE DATE]. This
offer will expire if not accepted by that date.

We are excited about the possibility of you joining our team. If you have any
questions, please contact [HR Contact] at [email/phone].

Sincerely,

_________________________
[Hiring Manager Name]
[Title]
[Company Name]

---

## ACCEPTANCE

I accept this offer of employment and agree to the terms stated above.

Signature: _________________________

Printed Name: _________________________

Date: _________________________

Anticipated Start Date: _________________________
```

---

## Best Practices

### Do’s
- **Consult legal counsel** — Employment law varies by jurisdiction
- **Keep copies signed** — Document all agreements
- **Update regularly** — Laws and policies change
- **Be clear and specific** — Avoid ambiguity
- **Train managers** — On policies and procedures

### Don’ts
- **Don’t use generic templates** — Customize for your jurisdiction
- **Don’t make promises** — That could create implied contracts
- **Don’t discriminate** — In language or application
- **Don’t forget at-will language** — Where applicable
- **Don’t skip review** — Have legal counsel review all documents

---

## Additional Resources Referenced

- SHRM – employment templates
- Department of Labor
- EEOC Guidance
- State-specific labor departments
